title: Introduction to rsxr
text: RAD-seq sex-determination analyses need marker depth tables, group contrasts, significance Bayesian triage. rsx engine implements steps streaming, bounded-memory commands stable C API. rsxr binds C API directly R (subprocess), pipelines can call process, freq, distrib, signif, triage, depth, merge, pca without leaving R, consume results tibbles via marker_table(). Target users R-first bioinformaticians already work popmaps marker TSVs (including outputs compatible classic RADSex workflow) want -process R entry point Rust implementation.

title: Introduction to rsxr
text: rsxr lives rsx-r/ subdirectory rsx-rs monorepo requires Rust toolchain (cargo, rustc; see https://rustup.rs) plus rsxcore sources sibling package directory (default full clone). local clone monorepo: Set RSX_CORE_DIR rsxcore ../rsxcore relative package.
code: # pak (recommended) pak::pak("HaoZeke/rsx-rs/rsx-r")  # remotes remotes::install_github("HaoZeke/rsx-rs", subdir = "rsx-r") cd rsx-r R CMD INSTALL . # or: pixi run install

title: Introduction to rsxr
text: function mirrors one rsx CLI command returns output path invisibly:
code: library(rsxr)  rsx_version()  # After demultiplexed FASTQ files exist under reads/: rsx_process("reads/", "markers.tsv", threads = 8L, min_depth = 5L) rsx_freq("markers.tsv", "freq.tsv", min_depth = 5L) rsx_signif(   "markers.tsv", "popmap.tsv", "signif.tsv",   test = "fisher", correction = "fdr", bayes = TRUE ) rsx_triage("markers.tsv", "popmap.tsv", "triage.tsv", min_depth = 10L)

title: Introduction to rsxr
text: marker_table() holds path (writes data frame temp TSV). Verbs run corresponding command temporary file return tibble:
code: mt <- marker_table("markers.tsv")  triaged <- triage(mt, popmap = "popmap.tsv", min_depth = 10L) sig     <- signif_markers(mt, popmap = "popmap.tsv", test = "fisher") dist    <- distrib(mt, popmap = "popmap.tsv", group1 = "M", group2 = "F") freqs   <- frequencies(mt, min_depth = 5L) depths  <- depth(mt, popmap = "popmap.tsv")

title: Introduction to rsxr
text: Runtime build: cargo rustc (see Config/rsxr/MSRV DESCRIPTION). Compression libs used Rust stack: zlib, bzip2, xz (usually present CRAN builders; install -dev packages Linux linking fails). Release tarballs may ship vendored Rust crates src/rust/vendor.tar.xz CRAN can build offline; developer clones without vendoring build online -repo rsxcore path dependency.

title: Authors and Citation
code: rsxr links against the rsxcore Rust library and, in a CRAN build, bundles its Rust dependency tree under src/rust/vendor (compressed as vendor.tar.xz).  The bundled crates are third-party Rust packages distributed under permissive licenses (predominantly MIT or Apache-2.0). A machine-readable manifest of the exact vendored crates, versions, and licenses is produced by tools/vendor.sh (via cargo-about, written to inst/AUTHORS.json) at packaging time and ships in the source tarball.  rsxcore and these bindings are released under GPL-3.0-or-later.  Upstream: - rsxcore: https://github.com/HaoZeke/rsx-rs (Rohit Goswami, Ruhila Goswami) - needletail, flate2, rayon, and the rest of the dependency tree: see the   vendored Cargo.lock and inst/AUTHORS.json.
